about.title: Sutter Creek Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Sutter Creek's historic downtown along Main Street draws visitors to its wooden storefronts, uneven sidewalks, and older building entrances — charming, but also the kind of terrain where a poorly maintained step or a wet floor left unaddressed can lead to a serious fall. Whether it happened at a shop near Main Street, a business off Ridge Road, or a property near Rt 49, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix or warn about it? That's the heart of a premises liability claim. We evaluate what happened, help you preserve evidence like surveillance footage, and explain your options under a contingency fee arrangement, meaning there's no cost unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Getting Legal Help Early Matters

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. We can help gather maintenance records, prior complaints, or inspection logs to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of video can make the difference in showing exactly how the hazard formed and how long it existed.

items.title: Your Deadline and Your Fault Percentage Both Matter
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a premises liability claim in California, less if a government entity owns the property, and any comparative fault assigned to you can reduce — but not automatically bar — your recovery.

items.question: I fell on a sidewalk near a shop on Main Street in Sutter Creek. Who's responsible?
items.answer: Responsibility depends on who owns or controls that section of sidewalk — it could be the business, a private property owner, or the city, and each has different rules and deadlines. We can help determine the right party and, if it's a public entity, note that the filing window may be shorter than the standard two years.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the hazard, note the date and time, and try to identify any witnesses before they leave. Reporting the incident to the property manager or business and asking that they preserve any surveillance footage can also protect key evidence.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to us about your slip and fall claim?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money. There's no upfront cost or obligation to see if you have a viable claim.
